questions.question:
After interchanging which two signs, the value of the given equation will be '1'?

3 ÷ 1 + 6 × 2 - 5
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4671232025562bc3ba9a781319d633acf8cd8e78dc8e96912cd7564a7df4717d.png] 

Option 1) : + and -

Given equation is : 3 ÷ 1 + 6 × 2 - 5 = 1

After interchanging the two signs the equation is as follows : 3 ÷ 1 - 6 × 2 + 5 = 1

⇒ __**3 ÷ 1**__ - 6 × 2 + 5 = 1

⇒ 3 - __**6 × 2**__ + 5 = 1

⇒ __**3**__ - 12 __**+ 5**__ = 1

⇒ __**8 - 12**__ = 1

⇒ -4 ≠ 1

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) : ÷ and +

Given equation is : 3 ÷ 1 + 6 × 2 - 5 = 1

After interchanging the two signs the equation is as follows : 3 + 1 ÷ 6 × 2 - 5 = 1

⇒ 3 + __**1 ÷ 6**__ × 2 - 5 = 1

⇒ 3 + __**0.166 × 2**__ - 5 = 1

⇒ __**3 + 0.33**__ - 5 = 1

⇒ __**3.33 - 5**__ = 1

⇒ -1.66 ≠ 1

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : × and -

Given equation is : 3 ÷ 1 + 6 × 2 - 5 = 1

After interchanging the two signs the equation is as follows : 3 ÷ 1 + 6 - 2 × 5 = 1

⇒ __**3 ÷ 1**__ + 6 - 2 × 5 = 1

⇒ 3 + 6 - __**2 × 5**__ = 1

⇒ __**3 + 6**__ - 10 = 1

⇒ __**9 - 10**__ = 1

⇒ -1 ≠ 1

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) : ÷ and × 

Given equation is : 3 ÷ 1 + 6 × 2 - 5 = 1

After interchanging the two signs the equation is as follows : 3 × 1 + 6 ÷ 2 - 5 = 1

⇒ 3 × 1 + __**6 ÷ 2**__ - 5 = 1

⇒ __**3 × 1**__ + 3 - 5 = 1

⇒ __**3 + 3**__ - 5 = 1

⇒ __**6 - 5**__ = 1

⇒ **1 = 1**

**LHS = RHS**

Hence, the correct answer is **"÷ and ×".**

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some L are G.

II. All M are L.

**Conclusion:**

I. All L are M

II. Some G are not M.

III. No M is G.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows
Both conclusions I and III follows
Both conclusions II and III follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca4f8ce41fd5fe95e695e15ef39f7ce28316b6095c99d6afa72e98a9837d29fb.png] 

Conclusion:

I. All L are M → False (As All M are L so, All L are M is false)

II. Some G are not M → False (As Some L are G and All M are L so, Some G are not M is not definite)

III. No M is G → False (As Some L are G and All M are L so, No M is G is false)

∴ Here, All three conclusion I and II and III are false.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Neither conclusion follows".**

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the Conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All P are M.

II. No P is R.

**Conclusion:**

I. Some R are not P.

II. Some M are not R.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows

questions.solution:
Statements:

I. All P are M.

II. No P is R.

The Venn diagram as per the given statements:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acb4e32676c382f7c88a007ee253570085f9f0a08804c24f057815ce381de5f7.png] 

Conclusion:

I. Some R are not P. →** Follow** (As no P is R means some R are not P is definitely true)

II. Some M are not R. → **Follow** (All P are M and no P is R means the part of P which comes in M is not R, so some M are not R is definitely true)

Hence, the correct answer is** "Both conclusions I and II follow".**

questions.solution:

**Logic: **Second no. = (First no. × 11)

**12 : 132 →**

⇒ (12 × 11) = 132

Similarly,

**16 : ? →**

⇒ (16 × 11) = **176**

Here, **'16 : 176'** is the correct pair.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option (3)".

questions.question: Six girls Priva, Muskan, Rani, Sirjana, Tina and Laxmi are sitting in a row facing towards south (not necessarily in the same order). Muskan is second to the right of Tina. Sirjana is second to the left of Tina. Laxmi is second to the left of Rani. Rani is to the immediate right of Muskan, Who is sitting to the immediate right of Priya?
questions.solution:
Six girls **Priva, Muskan, Rani, Sirjana, Tina and Laxmi** are sitting in a row facing towards south (not necessarily in the same order).

1. Muskan is second to the right of Tina.

2. Sirjana is second to the left of Tina.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6869b5bd8b903b8718858c8606bf6defd36f698ac091215b02b2d317a324fbe6.png] 

3. Rani is to the immediate right of Muskan.

The above condition cannot be satisfied in case II, so it is eliminated.

4. Laxmi is second to the left of Rani.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2efeea0bdc4dd3e6aeceac63c68aa65d606484f5163dddc5b9fd32039f8158d.png] 

Priva, the only person left will occupy the vacant position.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1e2d7dc6b32678c79366639045d7621d163348d223fe27b23d082ab5bfb74c88.png] 

Clearly, Tina is sitting to the immediate right of Priya.

Hence, ‘**Tina**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: Price of five cars C1, C2, C3, C4 and C5 are compared. Price of C1 is the least. No two cars have the same price, Price of C3 is less than C5, C2 and C4. Price of neither C5 nor C2 is the highest. Price of C5 is less than C2. Price of how many cars is more than the price of C4?
questions.solution:
Given : 

 
• Price of five cars C1, C2, C3, C4 and C5 are compared.
 
• No two cars have the same price

Explanation : 

1) Price of C1 is the least.

2) Price of C3 is less than C5, C2 and C4.

3) Price of C5 is less than C2.

As position of C5 is not known yet, therefore there are three possible positions.

 
• Case - (1) :

_ > C2 > C5 > C3 > C1

 
• Case - (1) :

C2 > C5 > _ > C3 > C1

 
• Case - (1) :

C2 > _ > C5 > C3 > C1

4) Price of neither C5 nor C2 is the highest.

As C2 cannot be positioned as the highest, therefore case - (2) and case - (3) are eliminated.

As only one position is left, thus will be occupied by the only car left i.e C4.

 
• Case - (1) :

C4 > C2 > C5 > C3 > C1

Thus, according to the final arrangement no car or zero number of cars have higher price than C4.

Hence, "0" is the correct answer.
